headline.text: Gross margin 56% (+200 bps yoy, +80 bps qoq)
Revenue growth is decelerating: guided 41% vs 50% reported
Management wording (confident vs cautious cues, -1..+1): qa +0.47

trajectory.name: Data Center AI (Instinct)

guided.text: In data center AI, the growing number and scale of Helios and MI450 Series Instinct deployments position the business for significant growth in the second half of the year with growth accelerating in 2027.

trajectory.note: guided figure read from the sentence, not yet in the ledger; no reported growth figure for this segment

tone.method: lexical cue counts on management sentences; indicative of wording, not a measure of business health

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We delivered another outstanding quarter with record revenue and profitability as adoption of our leadership products continued to expand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 50% year-over-year to $11.5 billion, driven by significantly higher sales of EPYC, Instinct, Ryzen and embedded processors.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Data center revenue more than doubled year-over-year and now represents 58% of total revenue, up from 42% a year ago, reflecting the rapidly expanding scale of our server and data center AI businesses.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Our record results mark another clear step up in AMD's financial performance and demonstrates the strength of our product portfolio and execution.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are still in the early stages of a multiyear AI adoption cycle as deployments grow across a broad set of markets and workloads, driving demand for more compute and creating a clear path to significant revenue growth and earnings power in the years ahead.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Data center revenue grew 107% year-over-year to a record $6.7 billion, driven by strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct accelerators.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In server, we delivered our fifth consecutive quarter of record server CPU revenue with cloud and enterprise sales each growing more than 70% year-over-year, exceeding the outlook we provided last quarter.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We gained x86 server revenue share year-over-year as customers expanded deployments of both fifth-gen EPYC Turin and fourth-gen EPYC Genoa families.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In cloud, hyperscalers continued expanding EPYC across their internal infrastructure and public cloud offerings, including AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle and others.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: That expanding footprint is translating into growing adoption of EPYC in the cloud with health care, financial services, media and technology companies adding tens of millions of instances last quarter.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In enterprise, we delivered record sales in our fourth consecutive quarter of record sell-through as on-prem adoption accelerated driven by the leadership performance and TCO advantages of our EPYC portfolio.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Growth was broad-based as we won large deployments with leading financial services, manufacturing, telecom, retail, and technology companies.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Our sixth-gen EPYC Venice family is purpose-built for this expanding range of workloads and delivers one of the largest generational performance gains in EPYC history.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Built on our all-new Zen 6 core and 2-nanometer technology, Venice extends EPYC leadership in performance and efficiency, delivering more than twice performance per watt of leading x86 CPUs, and up to 3.3x the performance per watt of leading ARM-based CPUs.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Venice is in production now with every major OEM on track to launch platforms and the leading cloud providers planning deployments beginning later this year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Customer demand for Venice is stronger than for any prior EPYC generation, and we expect to continue growing market share across cloud and enterprise in the coming quarters.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Revenue more than doubled year-over-year driven by strong demand for Instinct accelerators.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: MI355x adoption continued to broaden as leading AI companies scale deployments across a growing range of inferencing and training workloads and cloud providers expanded MI350-series availability.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: At our Advanced AI event, we launched Helios, our rack-scale AI platform combining EPYC Venice CPUs, MI450-Series GPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm software.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Across a broad range of inferencing workloads, Helios delivers up to 15% more throughput at the same rack power and up to 30% more tokens per dollar than the competition.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Customer pull for Helios is very strong and tracking ahead of our initial forecast.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In addition to our multi-generation gigawatt scale deployments with OpenAI and Meta, we announced a new strategic partnership with Anthropic.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Anthropic will deploy up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 series GPUs in Helios with deployment of the first gigawatt beginning in the first half of 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: The partnership includes a multiyear joint engineering collaboration using Claude to optimize workloads for Instinct GPUs and accelerate ROCm software development.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We also expanded our long-standing partnership with Microsoft.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Microsoft will deploy Helios at scale on Azure for frontier model inferencing across Microsoft, its AI customers and Azure AI services.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Together, these commitments broaden the group of leading AI companies and cloud providers building their next-generation infrastructure on AMD.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Helios is now in production with initial shipments on track to begin later this quarter and ramp through the fourth quarter and into 2027 to meet very strong customer demand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Looking beyond Helios, we plan to launch a new rack-scale AI platform every year with each generation delivering significant performance, efficiency and TCO gains.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In 2027, our next-generation platform combines MI500 series GPUs, Verano CPUs and Pensando networking with expanded scale-up domains in both copper and optical-based interconnects.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Customer engagement on MI500 is very strong with multiple customers working closely with us as they plan their next-generation AI infrastructure.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We expect MI500 to deliver the largest generational leap in Instinct history putting us on track to increase inferencing performance more than 2,000 times in just 4 years.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: ROCm has reached an important inflection point with the performance, capabilities and developer experience customers need to deploy AI in production at scale.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: More than 3 million models now run out of the box on AMD, the leading open models launched with day 0 support for Instinct and open source contributions to ROCm have increased more than tenfold over the past year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We introduced ROCm.ai, our new AI-assisted development platform for AMD GPUs last month.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: ROCm.ai lets developers use today's leading coding agents, including Claude, Codex and Cursor to create, port and optimize code for Instinct, making it significantly faster and easier to bring new models and workloads to AMD.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: ROCm.ai delivers more than twice the training performance and won 3x the inferencing performance of ROCm 7 across a broad range of models.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are also working closely with the leading AI labs, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and others to co-optimize ROCm for their models with the improvements benefiting the entire AMD ecosystem.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Taking a step back, the overall data center market opportunity is expanding far more rapidly than we projected just 6 months ago.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: As AI moves into production across a broader range of applications and workloads demand for both accelerators and CPUs is growing well above our prior expectations.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We now expect the data center AI accelerator market to grow more than 45% annually to approximately $1.4 trillion by 2030.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we expect the server CPU market to grow more than 50% annually to approximately $220 billion by 2030.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: For AMD, this larger opportunity, combined with the strength of our portfolio and growing customer visibility is creating a steeper growth trajectory for our data center business.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In data center AI, the growing number and scale of Helios and MI450 Series Instinct deployments position the business for significant growth in the second half of the year with growth accelerating in 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In server CPUs with very strong customer demand and improved supply, we now expect server revenue to grow more than 80% year-over-year in the second half of 2026 and more than 70% for the full year 2027, off a much higher base.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Taken together, we now expect data center segment revenue to more than double year-over-year in 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Segment revenue grew 6% year-over-year to $3.8 billion.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In client, revenue increased 23% year-over-year to $3.1 billion, driven by record mobile processor revenue and continued share gains.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Commercial adoption continued to expand in the quarter, with Ryzen Pro sales growing more than 50% year-over-year as we close new wins with large health care, technology, automotive, and financial services companies.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: To build on this momentum, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Asus and others launched a broad portfolio of new commercial PCs powered by our latest generation Ryzen AI Pro 400 series processors.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Demand was also strong for our Ryzen AI Halo developer systems, which went on sale in the quarter.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In July, we introduced our next-generation Ryzen AI Halo platform powered by our new Gorgon Halo processor, featuring an industry-leading 192 gigabytes of unified memory and can run models with up to 300 billion parameters.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And to make it even easier for developers to build and test large AI models locally, we are partnering with Hugging Face to include 1 year of Hugging Face Pro with every Ryzen AI Halo system beginning later this year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Looking to the second half of the year, we are planning for a softer PC market as higher memory and component costs weigh on demand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Against this backdrop, we expect our client business to perform better than the market, driven by the strength of our Ryzen portfolio and growing commercial adoption.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In gaming, revenue declined 31% year-over-year to $779 million, primarily due to lower semi-custom sales at this stage of the console cycle.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Gaming graphics revenue also declined year-over-year as higher industry-wide component costs contributed to higher graphics card prices and weighed on overall demand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 19% year-over-year to $977 million, our strongest growth in more than 3 years.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Demand was broad-based with strength across networking, aerospace and defense, test measurement and emulation and communication customers.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Our embedded x86 business grew significantly in the quarter as hyperscalers and networking customers increasingly adopted our CPUs to power critical networking and control plane functions in the data center.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We also continued to expand our portfolio, introducing Ryzen AI embedded x100 processors for demanding real-time edge AI workloads and the Kria AI robotics platform for physical AI.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Embedded x86 is becoming a significant growth driver for the segment.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Our overall embedded portfolio is outgrowing the market and gaining share, and our embedded semi-custom engagements are expanding.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Design win momentum also remains very strong.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are tracking towards another record year with more than $18 billion of new design wins, led by major wins with networking, data center, communications, tests, and aerospace and defense customers.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: In summary, we delivered record revenue and profitability in the second quarter, reflecting our strong execution and the growing adoption of our leadership products.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We entered the second half with strong momentum across our businesses.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: With Venice and MI455X now in production, initial Helios shipments set to begin this quarter, Ryzen Pro CPUs driving continued commercial share gains and our embedded segment returning to strong year-over-year growth.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: More than a decade of focused investment has given us the strongest and broadest product portfolio in the industry, deep strategic relationships with the companies driving the future of computing and a proven ability to deliver multi-generation road maps and ramp complex products at scale.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We now see the overall market for high performance in AI computing growing approximately 40% annually over the next several years, approaching $2 trillion by 2030, and we expect to grow well above the market.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We now expect revenue to grow substantially above our prior target of greater than 35%, and we expect to significantly exceed our $20 annual EPS target within our strategic timeframe.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are still in the early innings of a multiyear AI adoption cycle and the opportunity ahead is enormous.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are exceptionally well positioned to capitalize on this opportunity and deliver significant growth in the coming years.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Revenue increased 50% year-over-year and 13% sequentially to a record $11.5 billion, driven by continued momentum across our businesses.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: On a comparable basis, diluted earnings per share increased approximately 82% year-over-year, significantly outpacing our revenue growth and demonstrating our earnings power as we scale our business.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Gross margin for the quarter expanded to 56%, up over 200 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially, reflecting a favorable product mix and a growing contribution from our data center business.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Operating expenses were $3.4 billion, an increase of 40% year-over-year as we continue to invest in R&D to expand our AI silicon, systems and software capabilities to support our long-term growth opportunities.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Revenue was a record $6.7 billion, more than doubling year-over-year and up 16% sequentially.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Growth was driven by greater than 70% year-over-year increase in EPYC sales with record enterprise sell-through and robust demand across our cloud customer base.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Instinct sales more than doubled year-over-year with the continued ramp of our MI350 Series product as adoption broadened across the largest AI labs, cloud providers, leading AI start-ups, national labs and sovereign AI deployments.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.8 billion, up 6% year-over-year and 7% sequentially.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: The client business revenue was $3.1 billion, up 23% year-over-year and 6% sequentially, led by record mobile revenue.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: The gaming business revenue was $779 million, down 31% year-over-year, primarily due to lower semi customer revenue.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Sequentially, gaming revenue increased 8%, driven by higher semi customer sales, partially offset by lower Radeon shipments.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Client and Gaming segment operating income was $582 million or 15% of revenue compared to $767 million or 21% a year ago, reflecting continued investment in go-to-market activities and expanding product road map.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Embedded segment revenue was $977 million, up 19% year-over-year and 12% sequentially as demand continued to improve across end markets and the new design wins began ramping.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Embedded segment operating income was $386 million or 40% of revenue, compared to $275 million or 33% a year ago, driven by higher revenue and favorable product mix.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Inventory increased sequentially to approximately $8.5 billion to support strong data center demand.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: At the end of the quarter, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $13.1 billion.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: We expect revenue to be approximately $13 billion plus or minus $300 million.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: At the middle point of our guidance, revenue is expected to be up 41% year-over-year, driven by very strong double-digit growth in our data center segment.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Strong double-digit growth in our embedded segment and the decline in the client gaming segment with growth in our client business more than offset by significant double-digit decline in gaming.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: Sequentially we expect revenue to be up approximately 13%, driven by strong double-digit growth in both our data center and embedded segments and a modest decline in our client gaming segment with slight growth in client offset by strong double-digit decline in gaming.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: In addition, we expect third quarter non-GAAP gross margin to be approximately 56%.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: In closing, we delivered another outstanding quarter of revenue growth and significant earnings expansion, reflecting the strength of our execution and the strong momentum across the business.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: As data center growth continues to accelerate, we entered the second half of the year very well positioned to deliver continued profitable growth.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So look, we are certainly seeing a very, very strong compute market demand over both the data center accelerator as well as the server CPU.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: As we go forward, certainly, looking at our Q3 guide and our Q4 guide, we see very strong growth across both server and data center AI.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So we're seeing server grow over 80% in the second half of the year year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We're seeing very strong data center AI growth and that reflects into our 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: The way to think about it is both businesses are going to grow a lot.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And as a result, as we ramp the large strategic customers that we have on Helios in 2027, you would expect substantial growth in that business in 2027.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: We're actually very pleased with our gross margin progress in the first half of 2026 and our guidance for Q3 2026.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: The first thing is, as Lisa just mentioned, our server business is expanding very significantly with the increased TAM and the pace of our business continue to grow, which from a gross margin perspective is accretive to our overall gross margin.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: On the other side, you are right, the pace of data center AI ramp is also very important because from a revenue opportunity perspective, we see large incremental revenue opportunity from data center AI once it ramps not only added tremendous revenue for the company, but also gross profit.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: But overall, we actually feel good about how we can really navigate through the transition of the business and continue to improve our gross margin to manage the balance of the gross margin plus our Embedded business is recovering significantly.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: We actually think the Embedded business will give us additional tailwind on the gross margin side in 2027.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: So I feel really good about that.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Look, I think we believe that the server CPU is going to grow substantially in Q3 and Q4.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: The way I would describe it in terms of dynamics is we have been - we have very strong demand across all of our customers in hyperscale and enterprise.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we have been adding additional supply as we've increased supply throughout the year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So we are guiding the Q3 segment to grow sequentially double digits.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Both server and data center AI will grow nicely within that.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And then we should expect more growth for each of those businesses in Q4 with more supply coming on for server as well as for data center AI, the Helios ramp is just starting at the end of Q3, and it will be much more substantial in Q4, so that should sort of give you the picture - we think Q3 is certainly a strong quarter as we look at the strong very strong double-digit growth in the data center segment.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So as we look at the overall TAM, first of all, it's a very exciting time in the compute market.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: When you look at every part of our business, whether it's server CPU, data center AI or our embedded business and our PC business we see them all benefiting from the AI tailwinds.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And beneath that, I think in each one of the segments, we see an opportunity to grow above the market.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So from that standpoint, with our view of the TAM being greater than 40%, we are also saying that we will grow greater than from an overall revenue standpoint for the company.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: From an overall data center standpoint, I think we have given a little bit of color on 2027, we believe that the server CPU portion of our data center business will grow by over 70% year-over-year off of a higher base.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we believe the overall segment will grow by over 100%, so we'll more than double due to the data center AI ramping.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: The way I would describe it is we have supply to more than meet the guidance that we've talked about and the upside potential is there.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So I think from a Helios ramp standpoint, we're expecting a very significant ramp over the next couple of quarters.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So hopefully, that gives you a little bit of color on how that data center AI will play out.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And in terms of the revenue per gigawatt, I think we've said double-digit billions.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: There is very good visibility into HBM allocation for what we expect to deliver in 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And the other piece of it is in terms of the memory bandwidth and the memory capacity, it is one of the advantages of the AMD solutions, when you think about the larger model sizes, they really benefit from the larger memory footprint, and that goes into the total cost of ownership.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So if you just look at our Q2 performance, when we said we grew over 70% in both cloud and enterprise, we actually had double-digit growth in both units and ASPs, but it was actually more unit.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: I mean we're seeing just very strong demand from an overall market standpoint.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: But as we go forward, you should expect both unit and ASP growth.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we're seeing that play out through this year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So Josh, when I was talking about Helios was ahead of our initial forecast, it was as it relates to the overall volumes.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So the amount of demand there is for Helios in 2027.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So what we're seeing from every one of our customers who's had a chance to not only spend time with Helios, but also spend time in our overall ecosystem, there is a high confidence that Helios will be a great addition to the AI portfolio, particularly around inference, and that was my comment about higher than our initial expectations.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: It's the fastest-growing piece.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And I think the thing that is very strong about our portfolios is we believe we can grow in every one of those segments.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So whether you're talking about per core performance or you're talking about overall socket performance and that gives us a very strong position across general purpose, agentic-AI and also the head nodes for the AI accelerator business.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So from our standpoint, when we look at our customer traction and our customer momentum going from Turin into Venice, Turin was already extremely widely used, especially amongst the hyperscalers.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: What we're seeing is when we go into Venice, the workloads actually expand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So there are more workloads that are going to be run on the next generation of EPYC than are run on the previous generation.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And that's what gives us the confidence to say that we can grow substantially ahead of the market given the product positioning.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: As it relates to our client business in 2026, I think our first half performance has been very strong.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And although we are expecting that the market will decline in the second half, the market has actually held up better than most people would have thought.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So our view is we will - we see the growth in 2026 on a year-over-year basis.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And as we go into 2027, I think we have a strong product portfolio that is coming on board to address not just the traditional notebook and desktop markets, but also as you think about a more AI-centric PC experience like what we have been talking about with the Ryzen AI Halo.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So I remain optimistic about the PC market as an important way for us to reach a broader set of users and our ability to grow ahead of the market.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We're all watching the component costs and how that will play out over the next couple of quarters.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: But I think our portfolio and our rising content in enterprise are very positive for our client mix.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: I think when we talk about the acceleration, we are talking about the second half versus the first half.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: If you look at the first half, our data center business year-over-year growth versus the second half, we do think there's an acceleration.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And yes, the server CPU we're saying is more than 70%, which we think at this point is a very strong statement just given where the business is.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we do expect the overall data center business to be well over 100%.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And the well over 100% comes because the data center AI business is going to be well over 100% just given the strength of our strategic customers, the ramp of Helios and all of the things that we've talked about.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: There are lots of customers who are interested in Helios at a more regular scale than gigawatt scale.

confident: anything that would give us pause

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Well, Jim, I don't think we see anything that would give us pause about hitting the targets.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: I mean we feel very good about the targets.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Now when you ask me what the range could be, there is a range, and the range will depend on the ability to bring on more capacity in a timely fashion.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So ensuring that we have the entire - our silicon CPU, GPU, networking components that go into it, all of the Helios components, I think we feel very, very good about that part of the supply chain.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And that gives us strong confidence in what we've guided for the data center AI business so far.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we're going to be continuing to look at how to accelerate some of those builds.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We are seeing every day more opportunities with operators to accelerate some of that capacity, and that's much of the work that we're doing together with our customers and partners.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And as we go through the next couple of quarters, we expect to continue growing Helios quarter-by-quarter.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: But overall, when we think about this, we are actually very optimistic about how we manage the ramp of the MI450.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: At the same time, with the server business continuing to improve and grow significantly in 2027, overall, I think they have a good offset.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: But I do think it's important to remember we have multiple other levers from the company perspective, not only embedded business, but also client business; we continue to improve gross margin and the operations team continues to do a great job.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: I would say the server CPU supply chain is tight right now, and it has been tight for the first half of the year because much of this demand was unforecasted.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And so we would expect that the 2027 server supply situation should be better than 2026.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: We feel very good about being able to satisfy what we just talked about, which was over 70% year-over-year growth.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And I believe depending on how things play out, there may be opportunities for that growth to go higher as we get through the next few quarters.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And so that gives us the opportunity to, again, work very hard on ensuring that we get the supply necessary to meet the very strong customer demand.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: But we feel good about where we are to satisfy both the strong ramp in servers as well as the strong ramp in the data center AI business.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: So I think the inference market overall is growing very substantially over this year into next year.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And so with our partnership with Cerebras, I think they have great technology.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: Together with Helios Plus and their wafer-scale engine, we get a very good solution for customers.

signals.speaker: Dr. Lisa Su
signals.sentence: And we would expect that solution to start becoming available in Q4 in the Cerebras cloud and extend into 2027.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: I think Lisa talked about the TAM growth at 40%, and we'll be growing faster than TAM.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: From an OpEx perspective, we'll continue to invest given the large opportunities we have ahead of us.

signals.speaker: Jean Hu
signals.sentence: But you should expect us to manage this OpEx increase to be less than the top line revenue growth.
